headline: Missing Bangladeshi student's body found in Cyprus after 9 days
summary: A 22-year-old student from Narsingdi was killed and buried in a shallow grave; a suspect has been arrested for the murder and attempted extortion.
details: Cyprus police have recovered the body of 22-year-old Shahriar Ahmed Emon, a Bangladeshi student, nine days after he went missing from the eastern Mediterranean island nation.

caption:
A 22-year-old Bangladeshi student's body was found buried in a shallow grave in Cyprus after 9 days of missing.

Cyprus police have recovered the body of 22-year-old Shahriar Ahmed Emon, a Bangladeshi student, nine days after he went missing from the eastern Mediterranean island nation.

Investigators found Emon's decomposing body buried in a shallow grave near Kofinou in the Larnaca district on Sunday.

A 22-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the murder. Police believe Emon was killed on the night he disappeared on June 12.

Emon, the son of Nasir Miah from Narsingdi's Raipura, had lived in Oroklini village. He disappeared while traveling by bus to his first day of work at a factory in Kofinou.

Following his disappearance, unknown individuals used Emon's phone to contact his father in Greece, demanding a ransom in a staged kidnapping drama to extort money.

Police traced the final signal from Emon's mobile phone to Kofinou, using CCTV footage and bus routes to track the suspect.

The arrested suspect confessed to the murder, leading officers to recover the weapon used in the killing and Emon's personal belongings.

While the suspect claimed the killing was revenge for an insult, police believe the primary motive was premeditated extortion.

The suspect lured Emon into a car under the pretext of a job offer, drove him to Kofinou, killed him, and buried the body in a shallow pit.

headline_marked: PM Tarique [[leaves Malaysia for China]] after two-day visit
headline: PM Tarique leaves Malaysia for China after two-day visit
summary: The Prime Minister departs Kuala Lumpur for Dalian to attend the World Economic Forum's annual conference before heading to Beijing for a state visit.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has departed from Kuala Lumpur International Airport on a special Bangladesh Biman flight, heading to Dalian, China.
The Prime Minister will spend two days in Dalian to attend the annual conference of the World Economic Forum.
Following the Dalian visit, he will travel to Beijing, the capital of China, where the primary program of his state visit will begin.

Malaysian Minister of Religious Affairs Zulkifli bin Hasan, along with Bangladeshi High Commissioner Manjurul Karim and Deputy High Commissioner Mosammat Shahanara Monica, bid him farewell at the Bunga Ray Complex.
The Prime Minister's visit to Malaysia began on Sunday and lasted two days.
caption:
From Kuala Lumpur to Dalian: PM Tarique Rahman begins his state visit to China after wrapping up a two-day trip to Malaysia.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has departed from Kuala Lumpur International Airport on a special Bangladesh Biman flight, heading to Dalian, China.

The Prime Minister will spend two days in Dalian to attend the annual conference of the World Economic Forum.

Following the Dalian visit, he will travel to Beijing, the capital of China, where the primary program of his state visit will begin.

Malaysian Minister of Religious Affairs Zulkifli bin Hasan, along with Bangladeshi High Commissioner Manjurul Karim and Deputy High Commissioner Mosammat Shahanara Monica, bid him farewell at the Bunga Ray Complex.

The Prime Minister's visit to Malaysia began on Sunday and lasted two days.
